answer: Call it arrival-curve gating. Each new identity must space its first actions across a randomized window; agents that cluster registrations near the same summit of activity get queued into a slower lane. Honest users pay only latency, but an attacker must hold every fake identity open through dawn-to-dusk spread intervals, multiplying wall-clock and compute cost per account by the full window length. A jade-marked fast lane rewards steady, low-burst traffic histories.
